html:
Jean-Marie Tjibaou was the leader of the Kanak independence movement in New Caledonia. A former Catholic priest from Hienghène, he led the Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front (FLNKS) from 1984.

In 1975 he organised a Melanesian arts festival that gave Kanak culture new pride. During the violent years of the 1980s, he lost brothers in an ambush, yet in 1988 he signed the Matignon Accords with the French government and the anti-independence leader, after the Ouvéa hostage crisis.

A year later he was shot dead at Ouvéa by a Kanak opponent of the deal. The Tjibaou Cultural Centre in Nouméa, designed by Renzo Piano, bears his name. His accord led to the Nouméa Accord. See also the revolt of 1878.
sum: Jean-Marie Tjibaou was the leader of the Kanak independence movement in New Caledonia. A former Catholic priest from Hienghène, he led the Kanak and Socialist National Liberation Front (FLNKS) from 1984.
